verdict.rationale: GitBook's first-party docs say it offers interactive API playgrounds. Its OpenAPI docs say users can 'test endpoints right on the page with interactive blocks' generated from an added OpenAPI specification. This covers the core of the story: readers trying API calls from within the reference docs. Missing for 10: in-depth documentation of how the playground runs real calls (authentication, environments/servers, CORS/proxying), and independent or hands-on corroboration that live requests work.
